## Two: what your movement is, and it is not a bigger room

**Movement Five is the second half of the turn's cost, and the finding the outline of record declares for it is this: a person who has heard a refusal is as unenterable as the person who said it, and the cost falls on both of them, and neither of them can be shown what the other one has, and there is no form anywhere in this empire in which either of them is entered as the one who heard a thing or as the one who refused one.** It is a cost and not a cure, it is spent in ordinary rooms on ordinary people, and it resolves nothing.

**What you inherit and did not pay.** A man of about sixty-one has moved a tin of two pens four inches along a stone in a fortnight and cannot say why and was not asked, and about three feet of that sill has been empty since. A girl of nineteen has been standing at that empty end of it at the third hour every morning for about eight weeks, **and in the last week of Batch 0004 the man at the other end of it said the first thing either of them has ever said to the other, and she cannot be shown to have been standing there on purpose and he cannot be shown not to have noticed her on purpose, and neither of them is going to be told anything and neither of them is going to be thanked.** A woman of fifty-three has said out loud that she is not going to stand at that end again, and does the second copy of that week's minutes on her own hand. A courier has put a satchel down where a person could have taken it three times in a fortnight and nobody took it. A woman of thirty-four has gone past a wall board twice a day for a fortnight and stopped at it neither time, and the fourth item on it is in her own hand and is not coming down. A woman at the foot of a stranger's stair has started a floor at the far end so that a passage can be seen through and be empty. A man of thirty-eight has looked into a looking-glass for the first time in about two years and left it face up on a table.

**What your movement may not do, which is your own list.** You may not resolve anything. You may not thank, forgive or send for anybody. **You may not create a form, a column, a heading, a roll, a list or a notice, and in particular not a form for a person who has stood somewhere, not a form for a person who has heard a thing, and not a form for a person who has said one.** You may not rule the fifth column and you may not pick up the question on the shelf. You may not put two people who must never be in one room in one room, and you may not state or deny a distance between any two of the people the state layer keeps apart. You may not walk either road or the four hundred yards and you may not enter the room with the rail at the far end of that run. **You may not take either paper out of that coat, and no hand goes into that pocket, and the coat goes back on the nail at the end of every working morning and the two things in it are on opposite sides of a seam and neither has been out in twelve volumes.**

**And the three prohibitions that are specific to Movement Five, from the outline of record:** it may not have anybody thanked; it may not make the standing a practice with a name; **it may not have the reader of seventeen or the girl of seventeen spoken to, thanked or sent for, and it may not give the girl the chance to say no about anything; it may not put the man of about fifty-five with a chain in a list with the four who cannot make sense of a paragraph, and it may not put the man of about sixty-one in any room other than his own; and it may not put the protagonist in that building off the old river road.**

**And the things that are spent and may not be repeated, undone or improved: a sheet that was on the boards at the second hour and that nobody put there; a third place made under the floor of a woman's own room; a man of thirty-eight deciding not to cut a line into a printed strip and hanging his coat on a nail; a man going out of his building for about four hours with nothing in his hands; a lamp that came with the room he takes by the week and has never been lit in about two years; a coin out of a door that is not going to be spent; a mat on a landing; a tin moved four inches along a stone; a satchel set down three times at the far end of a set of boards; a front of a ground floor started at the far end; a looking-glass put face up on a table; and the whole of what a woman went up a stair to find out, which is nothing.** **In particular, no chapter of your batch has anybody look in a coat, has either paper taken out of that pocket, has anything cut into anything, has anybody sent, and does not light the lamp.**

**And the refusal Volume 11 spent is not yours to touch: the one said once, to a bar, in a passage, with nobody within nine hundred yards who could hear a word of it. It is not repeated, not answered, not delivered and not improved, and the tin of oil is still standing on those flags about nine foot off that bar and neither of them has opened it, and the woman of about twenty-six at that lock is in no chapter of your batch and is not going to be told anything.**

## Three: the rooms, the floor, and the object

**Your movement stands in three rooms and the other three are available and are not necessary.** **The building off the old river road**, entered from the lane above it, with the sill, the tin with two identical pens in it, the window with no pane in it, and the shelf carrying a question that does not finish and has her own name under it — this is the room your movement is about and it is the strongest of the three, and five of the last batch's ten chapters stood in it. **The room at the top of a stair**, where a courier goes four times a week and has been handed a thing every week for eleven years and has got nothing back and has never once been told what is in it, and where a woman of thirty-four has a board with four items on it behind the boards. **The ground floor of a rented house**, where a woman at the foot of a stranger's stair has started a floor at the far end so that a passage can be seen through. **The room taken by the week is the protagonist's only room, because he may not be put in the building, is not at the lock, is not in the shed and may not go up the four flights. The shed at the end of the lane off the Slade is available and Movement Five does not need it, and if you do enter it then neither person of seventeen is spoken to and the resistance is performed as an act and not as a sentence, and a chapter that cannot do that does not use it. The room with the rail at the far end of the four hundred yards is not entered and not described and is not the room the ending's final image is made of.**

**The protagonist's floor. He is on the page, in person or as a person whose absence has a named cost in the room he is not in, in at least three chapters of the movement, in person in at least two of the three, and his want is visible in at least one. His only room is the room taken by the week.** His absence may be priced in a room he is not in, and the room at the top of a stair and the ground floor of a rented house are the two available for that purpose.

**His object for this batch has to be a new one and it has to be in that room, and what is not a possibility is the coat, the wall, the nail, the latch, the door, the chair, the stool, the plate, the mat, the lamp, the coin, and the looking-glass — that last of those is spent as the last batch's object.** **The second hand's figures, about nine hundred sheets a year and the once-in-a-while that the writing above the mark is somebody else's, are on the page and are not his and are not his object either, and a chapter that puts those two figures in his mouth has moved the volume's subject into its climax room a movement early.**

**A room is referred to and not described, and no room is described twice in the batch in the same words, and no room is described a second time in the words it was described in in a closed chapter. The test is not whether a chapter refers to a room; it is whether the chapter's first paragraph would let a reader who had not read the earlier chapter still see the room, and if it would, cut it. Open on a person and on something that person did or did not do in the last fortnight. No chapter of your batch opens with a whole room.**

**And the three people the state layer keeps apart stay apart, and the reason is written here rather than left to a review: a merge does not need two rooms to happen, it needs two people and one mouth.** The protagonist and the book-keeper four hundred yards up the lane off the Slade, who are both thirty-eight and are two different men, are never in one room and never in one sentence. The woman who keeps a rented house's ground floor and the woman of about fifty-three who keeps minutes are never in one room and no chapter states or denies a distance between them. The woman of about twenty-six at the lock end, the woman of forty with a scuttle, and the woman who keeps minutes are never in one room. **And the man of about thirty-four with a fair hand and anybody else who is findable are never in one room, and he is the only person anybody could put a question to and you may not put one to him, and you may not print, confirm or deny the number in his head, and name him when you write that prohibition, because a prohibition a reader has to guess at is half a prohibition.**

**And this batch adds no new named figure and invents no new person.** If you find yourself writing a person because a plan needs somebody in a room, that is the failure, and the answer is a person who is already there. **Movement Five is the movement most likely to need a person who agrees with something, and the answer to that need is a person who is already on the page and who does not agree, and the resistance has to be an act and not a politeness.**

**And this is the standing your movement is most exposed to, and it is the same one the last movement was exposed to and it is worse, because your movement is a cost and a cost is the easiest thing in this project to write as ten weeks of quiet correctness.** **Someone in every chapter must want something in that room and come away not having got it.** A chapter whose two people exchange four flat lines and part is a chapter about a lid. **And a constituency is not a crowd: the moment two of the people who stand where things are said are in a room together for the sake of being in it, the movement has written a meeting, and a meeting is a body, and a body is a roll, and a roll is the thing the outline of record forbids by name. The last batch kept that and you keep it: the two of them in the room with the sill are there because one signs and the other carries an armful past it, and not one of them is there for the other, and that is exactly why it is a place and not a gathering.**

## Four: the calendar, and the figure you must check yourself, and the place this project keeps getting it wrong

**A month in this calendar is four weeks, and the day inside the week is second, second, fourth, fourth, restarting in each month. Every interval is a seven-day step from the one before it, and the interval is measured before the sentence is written and not corrected after. Never compute a month-count. No calendar month name and no weekday name goes into anything you write, including a card and a state file, and no chapter asserts which day of the week anything fell on. The last batch wrote the word *Monday* into two chapters and a month-and-weekday sweep found it and it was cut, and a named day is not a day in this calendar, it is a name.**

**Chapter 0590's own date line, on line five of `chapters/volume-12/chapter-0590.md`, is the date you derive from. One seven-day step from that line is Chapter 0591's date, and you re-derive it from Chapter 0590's line and not from this paragraph.** The ten dates of your batch are ten such steps and are derived and not predicted. **This prompt prints no second date and no tenth date, because a prompt that prints a calendar is a prompt that goes stale, and the last two batches carried that standing and honoured it.**

**A year name is written out in full at every occurrence and abbreviated nowhere, and the method for reading a year name is to count the word *after* inside it, because a year name is a substring of the year name after it.** Run `grep -o "the year after" chapters/volume-12/chapter-0590.md | wc -l` before you write your first chapter, take the answer your run gives, and **that number is the number every date line of yours carries until your own steps take you across a year boundary.** The last batch found the turn: it carried 8 on six of its ten lines and 9 on four, and the fourth was the first week of a new named year, and the outline of record deliberately refuses to say which chapter a year name lands on because an outline's forward arithmetic about a calendar is a prediction about chapters that have not been written, and an outline behind this one made that prediction and was two weeks out. **So: do the ten steps out yourself, before you write a word. If your own ten steps carry you across a year boundary, the name changes on the first date line after it and the new name is the one you are carrying now with one more* the year after *in it, written out in full at every occurrence, and the week is yours and is not taken from any file and not from any prompt. If your steps do not carry you across, nothing changes and that is a reading and not a decision.**

**Run both calendar numbers over your ten files before you close this batch — the day inside the week, and the number of weeks in the month — and restart the day check at every month boundary.** A check that runs one global cycle across your ten files reports a break at the first chapter of a month, and there is no break there, and the way that reports a break is the way that is wrong. **A month boundary will fall inside your ten weeks, because Chapter 0590 stands in the fourth week of the first month and the first month ends two chapters into your batch, and the check that finds it is the check you must restart.** `python3 tools/measure.py calendar --volume 12` groups by the ordinal word and **does not read the year at all, and it cannot tell you that three different named years are in the files it reads. Print the instrument's figure beside the page's reading and let both stand.**

**And the counters inside your chapters are the second half of this, and the last batch moved two of them against the date lines and got both right.** The date lines are the lattice. **A figure that counts weeks, a flower's age, a passage's number of weeks, a lane's count of visits, a room's number of years, a satchel's number of times down a stair — every one of them is derived from the date lines, and where a figure you have inherited and a date line disagree, the date line is the lattice and the figure is what moves. Do not move a date line to save a figure.** Three counters are live and they are named in the state layer: the lane is a weekly errand and Chapter 0585 was its twenty-fifth week, so Chapter 0595 is its thirty-fifth and no chapter may call it a fortnight; the man at the sill has been putting his other hand into that tin for about two months as at Chapter 0580 and about four as at Chapter 0590, so by your last chapter it is about five; and the courier's satchel has been down four flights four times a week for eleven years, which is about two hundred and thirty trips a year on this calendar and not a number any mouth should say.

## Five: the locks, and the six refusals that are specific to this volume

**The count of things anybody has asked out loud in this matter is seven, and it is seven at the last chapter of every volume boundary in the state layer and at the last chapter of this one, and the number may be printed in a state record, in a prompt, in a card, in the outline and in no chapter.** An asking is a thing put to a person out loud in a room by somebody who wants a thing out of the answer. **A question mark in a mouth is punctuation and is not an asking, and the two counts are independent. Nobody in your batch may be asked anything out loud, in a room, by anybody.** That is not a matter of tone. A question in this matter is a party, a party is a person, and that finding was said on the page in a closed chapter in about thirteen sentences and it is still the answer, and this batch may not improve on it, argue with it, or discover it twice.

*One:* **no notice, post, commission, warrant, office, new heading over anything, and no new form for anything.** *Two:* **no house, seat or office is named, no person from the series plan's antagonist ladder is named, no person from this project's ending of record is named in any capacity other than the ones already on the closed page, and no new final enemy.** *Three:* **no romance, nothing implying one, no quiet mutual commitment, no moment in a doorway, and no second person who is a second ear because of anything except standing there.** **No romance has begun in any volume of this project, the ending of record registers a domestic partnership through a clear hearing in the LAST movement of Volume 12, and that arc is not refused by this batch and is not paid early by it, and a movement about what a second ear costs is the worst possible place to put one.** *Four:* **no number that is not on the page gets printed.** The number in the head of **the man of about thirty-four with a fair hand** is not printed, not confirmed and not denied. The figure at the end of the cold passage is not printed. The figure on the bill at Lowcross is unpaid and nobody is liable. *Five, and this one bites hardest in your movement:* **no chapter states the mechanism that gets a person to a place where a thing is heard.** Your movement is about a place where things are said and it is forbidden to explain how anybody comes to be in it. *Six:* **no chapter tells anybody that they were in a room.**

**And the rest of the standing locks.** The two people in their boxes stay in them and the form that put them there is not asked to be void. The question in the second of the eleven books stays a question, carries no full stop, is not printed out in any chapter, and its author is not asked a second time. **The name at the foot of a struck line is not printed in your ten chapters, and the name of the hand that struck it is not printed in your ten chapters, and the disputed family claim is not printed in your ten chapters.** The four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are four and are not asked one question about a number, **and the man of about fifty-five with a chain is not one of them and never is, and no chapter of your batch puts him in a list with them.** A girl of seventeen and a reader of seventeen are unspoken to, unthanked and unsent for, and the girl is not given the chance to say no. The second half of a sentence begun in a doorway has still not arrived. The fourth item on that wall board is unresolved and your movement does not resolve it. The box of about four hundred blanks is not opened and the box is not the case. The drawer is not opened and no chapter of yours says which drawer the knife is in. The sixteen volumes and the list of fifteen on loan stay where they are and nobody produces the list. The wage of nineteen days of a crew's money stays in a coat about four miles off and is not paid. The young man at the loading end is not brought up that stair a third time. **The four hundred and thirty miles, the nine miles and the four hundred yards of cold flags are each walked zero times in your batch, and the room with the rail at the far end of that run is not entered and not described and is not the room the ending's final image is made of.**

**And the four figures that must not be confused, each with its own period.** About four hundred blanks **a year** go out of the case at the near end. About four hundred blanks **in total** sit in a box under the far end of the boards, never filled in, lid not off it in six years, **and the box is not the case.** About four hundred sheets **a year** carry a line cut into the printed strip along the top. About four hundred and thirty miles **of river**. **A period is the one of the three parts of a figure that no instrument in this project looks at. Read the period out loud before you keep a sentence.**

## Six: the craft rules that come before every measurement in this prompt

**One: the ban is on asking and not on talking, and a room with no contradiction in it is a defect.** Two people in a room may argue, refuse, explain, instruct, ignore each other, contradict each other and finish each other's sentences. **Every chapter carries at least one exchange in which another person resists what the point of view wants. A room is not a scene until somebody in it is contradicted by somebody else in it, and a movement is not a list of rooms.** **And the resistance has to be an act and not a politeness: a person who goes quiet, or looks away, or is pointedly kind, has not resisted anything.**

**Two: a chapter has a scene and not a description of a room.** A change of situation inside the chapter, a person who wants something in the room, another person in the way, and an ending that is a decision or a cost and not a description.

**Three: no chapter closes on a formula.** A closing line is written for that chapter and for no other chapter in the volume, and if the same sentence shape appears in two closings, one of the two is rewritten. **Read your ten closing lines in one column before you close and not as a similarity figure, because no n-gram measure in this repository can see a sentence written twice with a substitution every few words.** **And the last batch found a shape that no measure in this repository can see at all, and it is the one your batch is most likely to reproduce: eight of its ten closings were some form of *nobody is going to be thanked for it* or *nobody is going to be told about it*, written eight times with a substitution every few words, and every measure was satisfied at once. Read the column for that shape as well as for a repeated sentence, because a project formula is a shape and not a string.**

**Four: the hedge is not a voice.** *About* is kept where the imprecision is the point and where the figure is on the page, and is cut everywhere else. **A figure repeated in every chapter of a movement is a page figure and not a voice.** The last batch stood at about one *about* in every fifty-nine words, a fifth of which were the word used as a preposition and were not hedges at all.

**Five: the male lead is in the room, and the floor is a floor on the page and not a number.** The floor is counted by reading and never by a string. **In the last batch `grep -l 'Kest'` returned nothing across its ten files and `grep -il 'thirty-eight'` returned one, and the page carried him in three chapters, two of them in person, and the whole of what those two strings cannot see was two thirds of the batch's floor.** A ten-file check is not a smaller version of a volume-wide check; it is a different instrument, and the one thing it is good for is finding out what it cannot see.

**Six: the metrics are subordinate to the craft and are recorded after the last edit, not instead of the writing.** A check that returns zero is evidence of nothing until the shape of the damage it is blind to has been checked, and a blind check is written down as blind in the same record that claims it clean. A corrected figure is named as corrected beside the wrong one and never overwritten. **A sentence bound is a ceiling and not a target, the ceiling is 85 to 88 words, and the splitter must allow a closing quotation mark between the full stop and the space. The last batch's ten per-file maxima came out at 71, 76, 61, 64, 73, 74, 70, 70, 71 and 78, so leave yourself headroom under eighty and take a sentence apart at a conjunction rather than at a comma.** And **a batch's weight matters: the last four of this volume stand at 11,929, 10,549, 10,200 and 9,923, and a writer who pads to reach a number has written a longer batch and not a better one, and a writer who comes in under nine thousand should ask whether anything in the ten is thin and not whether the total is right.**

**Seven: a chapter title names a room, a person and a turn, and it is a title and not an inventory.** One name, one room, one turn, under about twenty-five words, and no title states the volume's finding and no title uses the superseded title of the series plan. **At twenty-five exactly you are on the line and the line's own word is *about*, so aim at twenty-four. The last batch had five titles at twenty-five or over on its first reading and cut all five, and none of its ten carried a figure, and if yours does carry one, check it against Chapter 0590's date line before you keep it.**

**Eight, inherited whole, because the most repeatable object in this manuscript is not paper:** **a chapter may have a person refuse something. A chapter may not have the same refusal made twice in the volume in the same room, and the refusals already on the closed page are not to be re-voiced in a new mouth. They are entered once, in the state file, and a chapter written from a plan names a room and a person and not a sentence somebody has already said in that room.** **And the most repeatable object of all in this batch is the *not being thanked* construction, which is the last batch's finding in section Six above, and a movement about a cost is where it breeds.**

**Nine, inherited from the last volume:** **a room with two people in it is not a body. A person who has heard a thing is not a witness. A second is not a quorum. A refusal is not a right until somebody can be shown having made it, and a right that cannot be shown is a thing somebody says in a room. Nothing in your movement may be counted up into anything, and a chapter that gathers people into a room to be addressed has written a hearing, and a hearing in this matter is a column with a date and a person against it, and this court cannot make one, and the whole of the last two movements is whether one can be made by a person and not by a court.**

**Ten, and this is the standing the last batch added at item 159, and it is the most expensive thing in this prompt: *the re-print check is the only instrument in this project that counts a word, and a batch can hold a dozen verbatim passages out of closed chapters while every instrument reports it clean — including an instrument that has been planted nine times, re-planted once, and run over five hundred and ninety files.*** **Run the re-print instrument over the whole manuscript and not over your batch, because a batch is ten chapters and a pair that crosses a batch boundary is invisible to every phase that checks its own ten.** **And run it over the PREVIOUS TWENTY CHAPTERS AS WELL, because the last batch's own instrument reported a clean zero over thirty files that did not contain `chapter-0574.md`, and a sixty-one-word lift was sitting in that chapter, and the repository's tool found it and named the file and the line. The set a re-print figure was taken over is part of the claim and must be printed beside it every time.** **And know what the last batch learned the hard way about writing the instrument: a guard in a matcher is a claim about which pairings are worth looking at, a guard written to save work will silently narrow the set, and a corpus sorted by name makes almost every partner sort before. Plant a case for the guard you write. Expect to lose plants to plants that were written wrong rather than to a wrong instrument.**

**Write your own detector, outside the repository, name it, plant it before you believe it, and re-plant it after you change it.** The detector the batch before yours wrote is at `/tmp/opencode/rep_12b4.py` and `/tmp/opencode/rep_12b4_fast.py` and **neither will be on the disk you are given, which is the reason and not an excuse.** The method is in full in `state/batch-summary.md` in the section headed for Volume 12's Batch 0004 and in items 153, 154, 155, 156 and 159: align by token value and not by index, extend every match to its full maximal length, compare a file against itself as well as against every other file, filter formula by the character span of every date line before tokenising, and de-duplicate by dominated position and not by merging. **Two plants that the last batch's set did not have and that you should write: one where the partner sorts before the focus file, and one where the run is longer than the plant.**

## Seven: what you run, when, and what you write when you close

**Run `python3 tools/measure.py selftest` before you believe anything else that tool prints.**

    python3 tools/measure.py selftest
    python3 tools/measure.py words
    python3 tools/measure.py sentences --volume 12
    python3 tools/measure.py reprints --window 20
    python3 tools/measure.py reprints --window 16
    python3 tools/measure.py markers

**And run the three that no tool here runs, one file at a time, before you close: `grep -o "the year after" file | wc -l` on each of your ten date lines, `grep -c '?'` on each of your ten files, and a month-and-weekday sweep at a word boundary over the twelve month names and the seven day names.**

**Write the batch summary, the ten chapter summaries, the continuity entries, the open-thread rows, the character-state rows, and the Volume 12 additions to the live header in `state/current.md`, and keep them compact enough that the next writer can use them cold.** **The bound, now met once and enforced again: a rolling file holds the open volume, the two previous batches and the standing locks; a closed volume, and the third batch back, is read in `state/archive/`.** **Volume 12's Batch 0001 record is already in `state/archive/` and Batch 0002 is now the third batch back, so your run's duty is to cut the five Volume 12 Batch 0002 blocks, whole, into five new files under `state/archive/` with a provenance heading and a SHA-256 per block, and leave every block above the cut standing. One open item lives in those blocks and it is named in the state layer: item 159 is in `state/open-threads.md` and is not in them, and if a later block carries an open item, name its new location in the provenance heading and print a pointer in the rolling file, because the archive's own rule keeps an open item in the rolling layer and this bound pulls against it.**

**Amend the live header and the ten lines under it in place, with the words they carried named beside the new ones, and send everything else to the archive.** That is the one exception the file's own convention makes and it exists because a hand-off is a working surface. **A figure in a state file is a copy of a figure and a copy is how this project's numbers go stale. The arrangement is stated once and is in `state/open-threads.md`. The cast is entered once and is in `state/character-state.md`. The canon is in `state/continuity.md`. The measurements go in one place, which is the batch summary, with the method named before each figure and the blind spot of each written beside its result and the command beside every number, and no figure from them is restated in another rolling file.**

**Never write a state file with an open-and-write idiom.** The batch before the one before yours truncated `state/current.md` from two hundred and four lines to one, because a single expression evaluates left to right and truncated the file before the call that was supposed to fill it raised. **Write to a temporary name, read it back, and move it over the file you meant to change, and then run `git diff --stat` before you close, because that is the method that found it and it is not an instrument in this repository.**

**Record, with the method named before each figure and the blind spot of each check written beside its result:** the ten word counts, the batch total, and the cumulative manuscript total; **the two calendar numbers over your ten files, with the instrument's own false break printed beside the page's reading, where the year turned if it turned and on which chapter, and the count of the word *after* inside the year name on each of the ten date lines**; the protagonist's chapters for this batch **by reading and not by a string**, with the chapter numbers and the sentence in each that puts him in the room, and the chapters that neither string returns and the sentence in each that prices his absence; the question marks, and whether any of them is an asking; the string sweeps, the month and weekday sweep, and the shared-run figures, each classified as formula or as prose before it is reported clean; **the re-print figures at both windows over the whole manuscript, over the previous twenty, and over your ten, and the first draft's figures beside the ones that survived for the re-print check and for the sentence maximum at least**; and **the ten closing lines read in one column, and what the column found that no measure found.**

**And what is not in this batch and may not be put in it:** the woman of about forty-three who bought a blank at that counter is a customer in a closed chapter and is not the woman of thirty-four who put the fourth item on that board herself; the man of about fifty-five with a chain is not the clerk of about fifty-three and no week is going to make him that; the box of about four hundred blanks is not the case; the four who cannot make sense of a paragraph are four and not five; **the protagonist and the book-keeper four hundred yards up the lane are two men of thirty-eight and a chapter that puts them in one lane is a chapter that has invented a person**; and the woman of forty with a scuttle is in no chapter of this volume. **And the decision that was unmade at Chapter 0550 is still unmade and no row you write may be read as having decided it in either direction.**

**Volume 12 is the last volume. Its last line is written by the phase that writes Chapter 0620 and by no other phase, and it may not be the last line of Volume 09 or of Volume 10 or of Volume 11, and it may not stand beside a second one. Nothing in this batch touches that, and the climax in the sixth movement is not yours and is one movement away and may not be reached early, and a chapter of yours that puts a hand in a coat is the sixth movement's whole act spent in the fifth.** A window with its catch turned and the window shut.
